SeedanceV3CallbackBody.description: Task callback body. Its shape differs from the query response; parse it separately.

event.description: Event type, always `task.completed`, same as the `X-DreamTo-Event` header.

taskId.description: Task ID, same as the `id` returned at creation.

status.description: Task result: `success` or `failed`. Note it differs from the query endpoint's `succeeded`.

result.description: On success, an array with the generated video URL (currently one element); `[]` on failure.

errorMsg.description: Failure reason; empty string on success.

timestamp.description: Callback time in UTC, RFC 3339, same as the `X-DreamTo-Timestamp` header; part of the signature input.

signature.description: Signature: `hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + taskId + "." + status))`, same as the `X-DreamTo-Signature` header. Empty when no webhook signing secret has been generated in the console.

SeedanceV3CreateTaskRequest.description: Request body for creating a video generation task. All fields are snake_case; only the fields listed here are accepted, any other field returns 400 "unsupported parameter: xxx".

model.description:
Model name, **required**: `seedance-2.5`, `seedance-2.0`, `seedance-2.0-fast` or `seedance-2.0-mini`. Supported durations, resolutions and media limits per model are listed under the values. An unknown model or one not enabled for your account returns 404 `not_found`. The value is echoed unchanged when the task is queried.

**Allowed values:**
- `seedance-2.5`: Seedance 2.5: 4–30 s (smart duration `-1` by default), 480p / 720p / 1080p, up to 30 images and 10 videos / 10 audios, honors `omni_reference_task_type`
- `seedance-2.0`: Seedance 2.0 standard: 4–15 s (default 5), 480p / 720p / 1080p, up to 9 images and 3 videos / 3 audios
- `seedance-2.0-fast`: Seedance 2.0 Fast: faster generation, 4–15 s (default 5), 480p / 720p only, no video editing / extension
- `seedance-2.0-mini`: Seedance 2.0 Mini: lightweight, 4–15 s (default 5), 480p / 720p only, no video editing / extension

content.description:
Input content array, **required**. Must contain at least one `text` prompt and may add reference images / videos / audios.

- Missing or empty: 400 "content must not be empty"
- No `text` item: 400 "content must include a text prompt"
- Media are numbered per type; reference them in the prompt as "image 1", "image 2", "video 1", "audio 1"
- Media URLs must be public `http` / `https` URLs or asset-library references `asset://<asset Id>`

The platform does not cap the number of items; the model does: `seedance-2.5` takes up to 30 images, 10 videos and 10 audios; `seedance-2.0` / `-fast` / `-mini` take up to 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audios. Exceeding a model limit makes the task end as `failed` with the reason.

ratio.description:
Output aspect ratio, default `adaptive`. Case-sensitive; other values return 400. When a first/last frame image is given, the output follows the input image ratio and this field has no effect.

**Allowed values:**
- `adaptive`: Adaptive (default): follows the reference image/video ratio, or lets the model choose for text-only prompts
- `16:9`: Landscape widescreen, for desktop, TV and most video platforms
- `9:16`: Portrait, for short-video apps and full-screen mobile
- `1:1`: Square, for social feeds and avatar-style content
- `4:3`: Classic landscape ratio
- `3:4`: Portrait ratio, for people and product shots
- `21:9`: Ultra-wide cinematic

duration.description:
Video duration in seconds. When omitted: `-1` (smart duration) on `seedance-2.5`, `5` on the other models.

- Integer from `4` to the model maximum: generate exactly that many seconds. The maximum is `30` on `seedance-2.5` and `15` on `seedance-2.0` / `-fast` / `-mini`
- `-1`: smart duration, the model picks 4 s to its maximum and you are billed for actual usage; the actual length is returned as `duration` when querying
- Decimals, strings or values outside the chosen model range: 400, e.g. "duration only supports 4-15 seconds or -1 (smart duration)"

Ignored when `frames` is also given.

frames.description: Total number of frames, a positive integer. Alternative to `duration`; when both are given `frames` wins and `duration` is ignored. Billed by actual usage. Non-positive or non-integer values return 400 "frames must be a positive integer".

resolution.description:
Output resolution, default `720p`. Higher resolutions take longer and cost more. `seedance-2.5` / `seedance-2.0` support `480p` / `720p` / `1080p`; `seedance-2.0-fast` / `seedance-2.0-mini` support `480p` / `720p` only. A value the chosen model does not support returns 400, e.g. "resolution only supports 480p / 720p".

**Allowed values:**
- `480p`: SD; fastest and cheapest, good for previews and quick iteration
- `720p`: HD (default); balanced quality and speed
- `1080p`: Full HD; best detail, slower and more expensive

generate_audio.description: Whether to generate audio (sound effects / music / voice) together with the video, default `true`. `false` produces a silent video. Must be a JSON boolean; the string `"true"` returns 400.

output_format.description:
Output container format, `mp4` when omitted. The platform only checks the type (string); whether a value is honored is decided by the model.

**Allowed values:**
- `mp4`: MP4 (default), the most compatible
- `mov`: QuickTime MOV, convenient for editing software

watermark.description: Whether to add a watermark to the video, default `false` (no watermark). Must be a JSON boolean.

seed.description: Random seed, an integer. The same seed with the same parameters usually produces similar results, useful for reproducing and iterating; when omitted the model picks one (returned as `seed` when querying). Identical output is not guaranteed.

camera_fixed.description: Whether to keep the camera fixed. `true` asks the model to avoid camera moves (no push/pull/pan), useful for product shots; when omitted, camera motion follows the prompt.

return_last_frame.description: Whether to return the last frame image. When `true`, a succeeded task returns `content.last_frame_url`, which you can feed as the first frame of the next clip for continuous generation.

bitrate_mode.description:
Output quality tier at the chosen resolution; omitted equals `standard`. Other values return 400 "bitrate_mode only supports standard / high".

**Allowed values:**
- `standard`: Standard bitrate (default, same as omitting)
- `high`: High bitrate; sharper detail and motion, larger files

callback_url.description: Notification URL called when the task finishes (succeeded or failed). Must be an `http` / `https` URL, otherwise 400 "callback_url must be an http/https URL". The platform POSTs the callback body to it; any 2xx counts as delivered, failures are retried after 1, 5 and 30 minutes. See "Task callback" for the body and signature verification.

tools.description: Tools to enable. Only web search is supported: `[{"type": "web_search"}]`, letting the model use real-time information. Anything else returns 400 "tools only supports web_search".

task_nickname.description: Task nickname, a string for your own labeling and lookup. It does not affect generation.

draft.description: Draft mode, a boolean. When enabled the model may produce a faster, cheaper preview. The platform only checks the type; the final behavior is decided by the model.

real_person_mode.description: Real-person mode switch, a boolean. When on, real people in reference images / videos are converted to virtual likenesses before generation. When omitted it is `true` on `seedance-2.5` / `seedance-2.0` and `false` on `seedance-2.0-fast` / `seedance-2.0-mini`; honored when the selected route supports it, ignored otherwise.

priority.description: Task priority, an integer. The platform only checks the type (non-integers return 400 "priority must be an integer"); scheduling is decided by the model side.

service_tier.description: Service tier, a string. The platform only checks the type; the behavior is decided by the model side.

execution_expires_after.description: Task execution timeout in seconds, an integer. Tasks still running after this time may be terminated by the model side. The platform only checks the type; the behavior is decided by the model side.

safety_identifier.description: Safety identifier of your end user, a string (pass a hashed user ID, never plain personal data). Used for content safety and abuse tracing. The platform only checks the type.

omni_reference_task_type.description:
Reference task type, honored by `seedance-2.5` only; other models accept a valid value and ignore it, deriving the mode from `content`. Other values return 400 "omni_reference_task_type only supports auto / reference / edit / extend". `edit` / `extend` need a reference video in `content`.

**Allowed values:**
- `auto`: Auto: derived from the media in `content`
- `reference`: Reference: generate a new video from the reference media
- `edit`: Edit: change the content of the reference video; needs a reference video
- `extend`: Extend: continue the reference video; needs a reference video

id.description: Task ID, prefixed with `task_`. Use it to query the task; the callback `taskId` carries the same value.

request_id.description: ID of this request (prefixed with `req_`), same as the `X-Request-Id` header. Include it and the task `id` when contacting support.

message.description: Readable error description that can be shown to users.

http_status.description: Same as the HTTP status code of the response.

request_id.description: Request ID, same as the `X-Request-Id` header; include it when contacting support.

param.description: The offending request field, present only for validation errors, e.g. `duration`, `content[1]`.

SeedanceV3ErrorResponse.description: Error response. Branch on the HTTP status first (retry / fix parameters / top up), then on `error.code` and `error.param`.

request_id.description: ID of this request (prefixed with `req_`), same as the `X-Request-Id` header. Include it and the task `id` when contacting support.

SeedanceV3ImageContent.description: Reference image. Up to 9 images; jpeg / png / webp / bmp / tiff / gif, aspect ratio 0.4–2.5, sides 300–6000 px, max 30 MB each.

role.description:
How the image is used. Case-sensitive; other values return 400 "content[n].role only supports reference_image / first_frame / last_frame".

**Allowed values:**
- `reference_image`: Reference image: subject, style or scene to draw from; multiple allowed, referenced in the prompt as "image 1", "image 2"
- `first_frame`: First frame: the video starts from this image
- `last_frame`: Last frame: the video ends on this image; usually paired with `first_frame` for a transition

url.description:
Media URL, **required**, either:

- a publicly reachable `http` / `https` URL (no auth, not intranet-only)
- an asset-library reference `asset://<asset Id>`: the asset must belong to your account and be `Active`; not ready, missing or deleted assets return 400 and nothing is charged

Other schemes return 400 "content[n].image_url.url must be an http/https URL or asset://<asset Id>".

SeedanceV3Task.description: Task object. Only `id` / `model` / `status` / `created_at` / `updated_at` are always present; other fields appear only when the information exists, so parse them as optional.

- `succeeded`: Succeeded; read `content.video_url`
- `failed`: Failed; read `error.message`

updated_at.description: Last update time, Unix timestamp in seconds.

duration.description: Actual duration of the generated video in seconds. Authoritative when the request used `duration: -1` (smart duration) or `frames`.

frames.description: Total frames of the generated video.

frames_per_second.description: Frame rate (FPS) of the generated video.

ratio.description: Actual aspect ratio of the generated video, e.g. `16:9`.

resolution.description: Resolution of the generated video, e.g. `720p`.

seed.description: Seed actually used; pass it as `seed` in a new task to reproduce a similar result.

priority.description: Task priority (when reported by the model side).

draft.description: Whether the task ran in draft mode (when reported by the model side).

video_url.description: Direct download URL of the generated video. Download it to your own storage soon after success; do not use it as a long-term URL.

last_frame_url.description: Last frame image URL, present only when `return_last_frame: true` was requested and a frame is available.

get.description: List tasks by filter, returning the status of several tasks at once. Only tasks created through this API with the current API Key are returned, newest first.

parameters.description: Exact filter on task IDs. Pass several by repeating the parameter (`filter.task_ids=a&filter.task_ids=b`) or comma-separating (`filter.task_ids=a,b`); the first 100 are used. Omit to list all tasks of the current API Key.

parameters.description:
Filter by status; omit for no filter. `queued` and `running` both mean in progress; any other value returns an empty list (no error).

**Allowed values:**
- `queued`: In progress (same as `running`)
- `running`: In progress
- `succeeded`: Succeeded
- `failed`: Failed
parameters.name: filter.status

post.description:
Submit a Seedance video generation task; choose Seedance 2.5 / 2.0 / 2.0 Fast / 2.0 Mini with `model`. Tasks run asynchronously: creation returns a task `id`; poll "Get task" or receive the result at `callback_url`.

The request example dropdown offers several scenarios (text-to-video, image-to-video, first/last frame, multi-image reference, video edit / extension, reference audio, web search, asset library…) that you can switch and try directly in Try it.

Requests rejected by validation create no task and are not charged.

Text to video.description: Generate a video from a text prompt only.

content.text: Photorealistic. Under a clear blue sky, a vast field of white daisies; the camera slowly pushes in and settles on a close-up of a single daisy with a few glistening dewdrops on its petals

Image to video (first frame).description: Animate an image used as the first frame.

content.text: Slow push-in, the person smiles, hair gently moving in the breeze, cinematic lighting

First and last frame.description: Generate the transition between a first and a last frame.

content.text: Smoothly transition from the first image to the second, steady push-in, soft light, cinematic transition

Multi-image reference.description: Combine characters, objects and scenes from several reference images.

content.text: The boy with glasses in a blue T-shirt from [image 1] and the corgi from [image 2] sit on the lawn from [image 3], cartoon style

Video editing.description: Modify the content of a reference video.

content.text: Paint the exterior walls of the house in video 1 blue and change the weather to snow

Video extension.description: Continue a reference video with new footage.

content.text: Keep the original camera move; the person keeps walking out of frame to the right as the light turns to dusk

Reference audio.description: Match the rhythm and mood of a reference audio.

content.text: The dancer from [image 1] dances on a neon street, moves synced to the beat of audio 1, fast cuts

Web search.description: Let the model use real-time information.

content.text: Make a short video introducing the most popular travel destination right now

Asset library reference.description: Reuse long-lived asset-library material via asset://<asset Id>.

content.text: The person in image 1 smiles and presents the product to the camera

Exact frame count.description: Set the total number of frames with frames.

content.text: An orange cat stretches on a sunny windowsill, slow motion

Smart duration + callback.description: Let the model pick the length, get a callback and the last frame.

content.text: Waves crash on the rocks at sunset; the camera slowly moves from a wide shot to a close-up of the spray

Seedance 2.5 long video.description: Generate up to 30 seconds in one task with Seedance 2.5.

content.text: The traveler in image 1 sets off from the foot of the mountain at dawn, passes through a forest and a stream, and reaches the summit at sunrise; the camera follows all the way

Fast / Mini drafts.description: Preview quickly with Seedance 2.0 Fast or Mini.

content.text: An iced coffee on a wooden table, ice slowly melting, sunlight through the window

get.description:
Get the status and result of one task. A task that fails during generation still returns HTTP 200 with `status: failed`.

Recommended polling: every 3 s for the first 30 s, every 5 s up to 2 minutes, then every 10 s; poll less often when you also use `callback_url`. Only tasks created by your account through this API can be queried.

parameters.description: Task ID, the `id` returned at creation (prefixed with `task_`). A missing or foreign task returns 404 `not_found`.
parameters.name: id

post.description:
When a task created with `callback_url` finishes (succeeded or failed), the platform POSTs this request to that URL. Any 2xx counts as delivered; failures are retried after 1, 5 and 30 minutes (4 attempts in total).

Callbacks only speed up notification: keep fallback polling and treat the query endpoint as the source of truth.

parameters.description: Callback time (UTC, RFC 3339), part of the signature input. Reject callbacks more than 5 minutes off your clock to prevent replay.
parameters.name: X-DreamTo-Timestamp

parameters.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature (hex), computed as described for the body `signature`. Not sent when no webhook signing secret exists.
parameters.name: X-DreamTo-Signature
